scope: Disposable local containers: one Supabase Postgres and one PostgREST, two environment databases; not a running installation.

checks.check: with no settings PostgREST serves public only
the settings in the environment database expose i2s without a restart
public is still the default schema
a schema that is not listed stays refused
the first schema listed is the default
the row limit applies
Studio reads the same values PostgREST serves
schema names holding a space or a newline do not make other names look present
the developer login cannot put an extension into the empty platform schema
a platform write naming a schema that is gone writes nothing
a drop that holds the lock first makes the platform write see the schema gone
a platform write that holds the lock first makes a concurrent drop wait and be refused
a schema named in the extra search path cannot be dropped either
a tenant session holding the lock makes the platform refuse at once, not wait
a start ends the tenant session that holds the lock, then writes
a start claims the lock past a holder and the sessions queued behind it
the guard refuses a schema drop at repeatable read
the developer login cannot change the REST login settings
the developer login cannot rename an exposed schema
the developer login cannot drop an exposed schema
the developer login cannot drop public while it is exposed
the API still serves after the refused changes
the developer login still renames and drops schemas that are not exposed
with no settings public is protected in another environment
the developer login cannot replace or disable the guard
a missing exposed schema makes PostgREST answer 503 to every request (why the guard exists)
at start a missing schema is left out and the rest is served
with every exposed schema gone the empty schema is served, not public
a reset returns to the container defaults
turned off, the API serves no table and public is not published
functions the tenant plants in public never run as the superuser
every guard searches the temporary schema last, and the presence check sees it
dropping an extension the tenant owns cannot take an exposed schema with it
a cascade through an extension the tenant owns cannot take an exposed schema with it
turning database access on again cannot run a function the tenant planted as the superuser
a start repairs a reserved-schema guard from before, which searched the temporary schema first
no environment keeps its settings in the catalog the cluster shares
tenant code that becomes the REST login reads nothing of another environment
tenant code that becomes the REST login cannot change what PostgREST serves
PostgREST applies its settings at a restart, not only after a reload
a platform backup restores the settings; a tenant dump of every schema still works
the presence check notices the REST login losing the pre-config function, and the guard gives it back
role settings tenant code gives the REST login elsewhere never reach another environment's export, and a start clears them
a connection that carries a PostgREST setting stops the configuration load; a clean one and a platform key do not
a settings save does not interrupt the API: no refused or missing table while PostgREST reloads
a database whose platform schema belongs to a non-superuser is refused by the guard
a database restored from before the pin is pinned again before REST starts, so PostgREST does not fall back to public
a tenant holding the REST login's role setting rows open delays the pin by seconds at most, and a start that ends the sessions gets through
PostgREST applies a settings write when its container is sent SIGUSR1, with no NOTIFY involved
a temporary table named record in the REST session cannot make pre_config set a platform key
a load that pre_config cannot make serves nothing, not public: the container falls back to the empty schema
a database from before the settings function (no sbarbase_rest, no empty schema) is made ready by the guard and then serves
a session search_path in a pooled REST connection, with unnest planted in public, cannot make PostgREST serve auth
a settings() that an archive brought, answering more than the three managed keys, applies only those
the developer login cannot put an extension into the schemas that hold the platform's functions
the Studio login's grants give up after the lock bound when a tenant transaction holds the tables, instead of holding the operation lock
a REST login whose password tenant code changed gets the platform's password back from the start's pin
a REST login session holding its own password row does not hold up the platform's password write
a function planted in public does not change what PostgREST loads, and without the REST search path pin the load is refused
applying the guard again keeps one enabled trigger
